title: Label and quantify mRNA molecules in live cell experiments using SunRISER and dNEMO
author: Guo, Kowalczyk, et al.

steps.title: Open dNEMO application
steps.instruction: Launch the standalone dNEMO executable by navigating to its folder and double‑clicking the icon, or, if using the MATLAB scripts, add the dNEMO_MATLAB_scripts folder to the MATLAB path and run RUN_ME.

steps.title: Load time‑lapse image
steps.instruction: In dNEMO choose File > Load Images, select the desired image file (e.g., SunRISER_SAMPLE_MOV.tif provided with the protocol). Supported formats are those readable by BioFormats; image size may be limited by available system memory.

steps.title: Test spot detection
steps.instruction: Run spot detection on the current frame and adjust parameters until spots are correctly identified.

substeps.instruction: Select ‘Test Detect (Full)’ in the Spot Filter panel to run detection on the displayed frame.
Toggle ‘Display All Signals in Current Frame’ to visually confirm detection.
Adjust the ‘Wavelet Threshold’ value (set to 2.25 for this protocol) and click ‘Test Detect (Full)’ again as needed.
Open Settings > Signal Parameters and set ‘Wavelet Level’ to 2 and ‘Frame Limit’ to 1; leave all other settings at their defaults.

steps.title: Create spot detection keyframe
steps.instruction: When detection is satisfactory, click ‘Create Keyframe’ in the Spot Filter panel to apply the current parameters to all frames of the time‑series.

steps.title: Run Cellpose segmentation
steps.instruction: From the dNEMO interface select Cell Masks > Run Cellpose; Cellpose will launch and segment cells across the loaded movie.

steps.title: Confirm imported cell mask
steps.instruction: After Cellpose finishes, a prompt appears; click ‘Ok’ to import the generated mask into dNEMO. Note that Cellpose does not provide cell tracking; tracking parameters can be adjusted later via Cell Masks > Adjust Import Settings.

steps.title: Optional manual cell segmentation
steps.instruction: If Cellpose is unavailable, use dNEMO’s manual segmentation: click ‘Add Cell’ in the Cells panel to draw a polygon around a cell, create keyframes to propagate the boundary across frames, and edit or delete cells via the Keyframes panel.

steps.title: Filter spots by intensity
steps.instruction: In the Spot Filter panel set the ‘Max’ intensity lower bound to 0.0075 (or another desired threshold) and click ‘Create Keyframe’ to apply this filter to the entire movie.

steps.title: Manually remove erroneous spots
steps.instruction: Open the Manual Removal panel, click ‘Remove Signals’, then click individual spots (or drag a box) to delete them; click ‘Update Removal Keyframe’ to save the exclusions and finally click ‘Stop Removing Signals’ when finished.

steps.title: Save analysis outputs
steps.instruction: Choose File > Save to output results; dNEMO will generate a .mat file and an Excel spreadsheet containing spot coordinates, intensities, and cell assignments.

steps.title: Run batch processing (MATLAB)
steps.instruction: Ensure the ‘batch_processing’ folder is inside the dNEMO directory and on the MATLAB path, then type RUN_ME_BATCH in the MATLAB command window.

steps.title: Configure batch processing parameters
steps.instruction: In the batch‑processing GUI select an input directory containing image files and an output directory, set detection and Cellpose parameters (or load a preset text file), choose which operations (dNEMO, Cellpose, or both) to run, click ‘Confirm Valid Input Arguments’ to lock settings, and finally click ‘Start’ to process all images; the right‑hand log window records progress.
